$comment: Recorded expectations for the graceful-degradation failure-injection exercise
after reviewing any diff. The runner fails on DRIFT — behaviour that changed
since this baseline was recorded — but not on a recorded UNGRACEFUL verdict,
which is a known issue rather than a new regression. Use --strict to fail on
those too, once the follow-up issues below are closed.
provisionalNote: PROVISIONAL — not yet confirmed by an executed run.
These verdicts were derived by reading the code, not by running the exercise.
Each one cites the specific lines it rests on in docs/chaos-engineering.md, and
the reasoning is checkable, but a code reading is not a measurement. The first
run on a machine with the backend dependencies installed and Docker available
should be treated as the real observation: review each result against the
analysis, correct any verdict that turns out to be wrong, and then delete this
flag so drift detection is armed for subsequent runs.

rpc-outage.evidence: sorobanMetadataService.js:53 dynamic-imports @stellar/stellar-sdk, which is not in backend/package.json; the throw is swallowed at :99 and returned as success:true.
followUp: Add @stellar/stellar-sdk to backend dependencies and stop reporting RPC failure as success (#839)

rpc-blackhole.evidence: sorobanMetadataService.js:57 constructs rpc.Server with no timeout and there is no retry or AbortSignal, so a silent RPC has no bound.
followUp: Bound the Soroban RPC client with a request timeout and retry policy (#840)

backend-crash.evidence: No SIGTERM/SIGINT handler for the HTTP server; index.js:1799 never closes the server. Only jobs/worker.js:66-74 shuts down gracefully.
followUp: Add SIGTERM/SIGINT graceful shutdown to the backend HTTP server (#841)

nginx-down.evidence: A dead upstream fails nginx's connect() immediately (502) rather than hanging, and the gateway resumes on restart.
followUp: Return RFC 7807 problem documents from nginx and set explicit proxy timeouts (#844)

redis-outage.evidence: index.js:607 calls buildTlsOptions() but index.js:21 does not import it; the ReferenceError is swallowed by the bare catch at :618, so /health reports 503 for any REDIS_URL.
followUp: Import buildTlsOptions in backend/index.js so /health stops always reporting 503 (#842)

health-ignores-rpc.evidence: index.js:595-598 declares only storage and redis as dependencies; the Soroban RPC is never probed.
